newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal rules out sending troops to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Portugal rules out sending troops to Albania.

text.p: Portugal believes conditions are not right to commit troops to a multinational force in Albania and doubts such a risky mission would succeed, Defence Minister Antonio Vitorino was quoted as saying on Thursday.
"I believe that at this time the participation of Portugal in the mission in Albania is not justified," Vitorino told Publico newspaper.
"The involvement of forces should require a set of military and political conditions. We (the government) believe that the political conditions have not been satisfied," he said.

"This is essentially an internal, civil, guerrilla-style conflict. And so there should be an acceptance of this foreign military intervention by those for whom aid is intended," he added. "I have not seen the necessary willingness of the Albanians to accept such a mission."
Asked if Portugal did not believe in the success of the mission, Vitorino said: "I believe it is a highly risky mission, and I have doubts it can reach its military objective."

Albania, already Europe's poorest nation, plunged into near chaos when get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed earlier this year and armed rebels took control of the south during an unchecked spasm of looting and banditry.
An Italian-led multinational force of some 6,000 troops, who will protect the delivery of emergency food and medicine supplies, is due to arrive in Albania early next week.
